claims.content: To monitor and confirm the status of all devices and facility components during scheduled normal operations to ensure they achieve their intended goal state (Open or Closed) as defined by the operational sequence.

goal.raw_text: To monitor and confirm the status of all devices and facility components during scheduled normal operations to ensure they achieve their intended goal state (Open or Closed) as defined by the operational sequence.

claims.content: Operator
The Operator must be logged into the RLCS system.
The system must be in 'normal mode' of operation.
All field devices and sensors must be connected to the RLCS network and actively reporting status.
A scheduled operational sequence requires an operator to be logged on to confirm each step of the operation, or a change in device status occurs that must be reported on the screen within 2 seconds.

trigger.raw_text: A scheduled operational sequence requires an operator to be logged on to confirm each step of the operation, or a change in device status occurs that must be reported on the screen within 2 seconds.

claims.content: The RLCS software monitors the status of all field devices.
The system displays and updates the database with the status of all system field elements.
Any change in device state is reported on the screen no later than 2 seconds from the time it occurs.
The system monitors field controllers and connected devices on the RLCS network for control system integrity.
The system reports any users logged in to RLCS network computers at any time.
The system reports all commands issued in the field units.
The system processes operator requests for changing field device status.

If no operator is logged on to the system, the status of all devices will continue to be monitored and displayed. If a scheduled operational sequence requires an operator to be logged on to confirm each step of the operation, an audible alarm will sound to alert the operator to log on to the system.
For alarm status, the GUI shall issue an audible alarm, and the icon shall be different from the okay status for that device. The visual alarm shall include a change of color for the affected device.
There shall be an option to turn off the audible alarm permanently or temporarily for a given period.
The alarm icon shall change to the normal status icon automatically when the alarm condition is removed. Alarm conditions shall be configurable on the screen.
When a device status has been overridden, on the screen it shall appear with different color from the normal and alarm status colors.
Critical alarms shall be generated when a closure device changes from a known state to unknown state (status lost).
Critical alarms shall be generated when a closure device changes from legal state to illegal state.
Critical alarms shall be generated when the control system Integrity verification indicates a verification failure.
Critical alarms shall be generated when a user logs in any of the field units.
Critical alarms shall be generated when a command to override a device has been issued anywhere in the system.
Critical alarms shall be generated when there is a communication failure within the RLCS network.
Critical alarms shall be generated when a computer in the RLCS network goes down.
Critical alarms shall be generated when there is a power failure at any controller or workstation.
Critical alarms shall be generated when a cabinet ID is changed.
Critical alarms shall be generated when the DCUs are in manual mode.
Critical alarms shall be generated when Watch Dog timer failure occurs.
Warning alarms shall be generated when security sensor activation occurs at either the FCU or DCU.
Warning alarms shall be generated when Air pressure, Temperature in cabinets, and Voltages are outside the limits of established thresholds as stored in the database.
If a critical alarm occurs during opening or closing operation, the system shall present the operator with possible actions that can be taken in order to complete the operation.
If overriding a device status is needed in order to proceed, the system shall determine if the operator has high enough security and provide advise on how to proceed.
The current status for all devices is maintained at each controller unit.
The database has been updated with the status of all system field elements reflecting any changes in device state.
Any change in device state has been reported on the screen no later than 2 seconds from the time it occurs.
Control system integrity has been verified, and any users logged in or commands issued in the field units have been reported.
If applicable, Critical or Warning alarms have been generated and displayed (audible/visual) based on specific conditions such as communication failures, power failures, or threshold violations.
